'''Nancy Sarah Goroff''' (born February 18, 1968) is an American organic chemist who formerly served as chair of the chemistry department at [[Stony Brook University]].<ref name="epmc">{{EuropePMC}}</ref> Her research investigates conjugated organic molecules, including polymers, halocarbons and buckyballs. During the [[2020 United States elections]] Goroff ran to represent [[New York's 1st congressional district]], and was defeated by the incumbent, [[Lee Zeldin]].

== Early life and education ==
Goroff studied chemistry at [[Harvard University]]. She moved to the [[West Coast of the United States|West Coast]] for her graduate studies, where she joined [[University of California, Los Angeles]], and worked under the supervision of {{ill|Orville L. Chapman|qid=Q15432822}} and [[François Diederich]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Confirmed Invited Speakers › Women for Women|url=https://www.w4w.nat.fau.eu/invited-speakers/|access-date=2020-10-02|language=en-US}}</ref>

== Scientific career ==
Goroff was an [[National Science Foundation]] (NSF) postdoctoral fellow at the [[Michigan State University]], where she worked in the laboratory of James (Ned) Jackson.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=Professor Nancy Goroff, former member of the Jackson Group, is Congress' first female scientist with a PhD.|url=https://www.chemistry.msu.edu/news/professor-nancy-goroff-former-member-of-the-jackson-group-is-hoping-to-be-congress-first-female-scientist-with-a-phd/|access-date=2020-10-02|website=chemistry.msu.edu|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Nancy S. Goroff receives award|url=https://www.chemistry.msu.edu/news/nancy-s-goroff-receives-award/|access-date=2020-10-02|website=chemistry.msu.edu|language=en}}</ref> At MSU she worked on the synthesis and study of [[carbene]]s. Goroff continued her postdoctoral studies at the [[University of Michigan]], studying chemical education with [[Brian Coppola]].<ref name=":2" />

In 1997 Goroff joined the faculty of [[Stony Brook University]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Nancy Goroff {{!}} Chemistry|url=https://www.stonybrook.edu/commcms/chemistry/faculty/_faculty-profiles/goroff-nancy.php|access-date=2020-10-02|publisher=[[Stony Brook University]] |language=en}}</ref> The Goroff laboratory designs [[Conjugated system|conjugated]] organic molecules, including polymers, halocarbons and buckybelts. Among these, Goroff is interested in [[organoiodine compound]]s (including iodoalkynes) and halogenated cumulenes. She has investigated the chemical, material and photophysical properties of poly(diiododiacetylene), a polymer known as PIDA. Goroff has shown that suspending solutions of PIDA in pyrrolidine results in the formation of a highly conductive material.<ref name=":0" /> Conjugated molecular belts, where the deconjugated π-system is shaped into a cylinder. The belts are not dissimilar to [[buckminsterfullerene]], a spherical carbon allotrope, but has open edges that can be functionalised further. These belts have potential for nanoscale switches.<ref name=":0" />

In 2013 Goroff was appointed the Associate Provost for the Integration of Research at Stony Brook University.<ref name="news.stonybrook.edu">{{Cite web|date=2013-09-13|title=Dr. Nancy Goroff Appointed Associate Provost for the Integration of Research, Education, and Professional Development and Associate Dean of the Graduate School |url=https://news.stonybrook.edu/newsroom/press-release/general/nancygoroff/|access-date=2020-10-02|website=SBU News|language=en-US}}</ref>

Goroff is a member of the [[Union of Concerned Scientists]].<ref name=":1" />

== Political career ==
{{Main|2020 United States House of Representatives elections in New York#District 1}}
In 2020 Goroff ran for the [[2020 United States House of Representatives elections in New York|2020 United States House of Representatives]], going on leave from her faculty position at Stony Brook University.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Nancy Goroff |publisher=Un ion of Concerned Scientists|url=https://www.ucsusa.org/about/people/nancy-goroff|access-date=October 10, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200901135304/https://www.ucsusa.org/about/people/nancy-goroff |archive-date=September 1, 2020 |language=en}}</ref> On June 23 she won the [[Democratic primaries 2020|Democratic primary]], with 36.1 percent of the vote, finishing ahead of 2018 nominee Perry Gershon. In November, she faced incumbent Lee Zeldin in the general election, losing by 9.8%.<ref>{{cite news |title=GOP Rep. Lee Zeldin defeats Democrat Nancy Goroff |url=https://www.fox5ny.com/news/gop-rep-lee-zeldin-defeats-democrat-nancy-goroff |access-date=March 28, 2022 |publisher=[[WNYW]] |date=December 4, 2020}}</ref> If elected, Goroff would have been the first woman scientist with a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] to be elected to [[United States Congress|Congress]].<ref name=":3" />
